title: Staged failover harmonizer with predictive cache prefill and fallback-variant degradation plan
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Our current cross-region fallback lacks a coordinated prefill strategy for KV/prefix caches and does not degrade model variants in a predictable, policy-driven manner. During region degradation we see higher tail latency and token-cost spikes when capacity moves to a fallback region because cold KV caches and aggressive model swaps cause repeated rework and circuit-breaker storms.

Goal: Implement a 'staged failover harmonizer' that coordinates: (1) predictive cache prefill/probe waves, (2) tier-aware traffic throttling during cutover, and (3) controlled fallback to cheaper model variants with progressive quality thresholds. The harmonizer should be policy-driven, observable, and reversible.

Non-goals: Not addressing full global active-active sharding; not changing the underlying kernel selection logic. This work focuses on orchestration and policy enforcement layers that live above the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Can run a simulated region disruption and move 100% of traffic to a secondary region within configured SLOs without >5% request error increase
Prefill wave completes within configured preflight window and achieves at least 80% KV hit rate for primed prefixes before traffic ramp
Model-variant fallback policy can be applied per-customer and rolls back automatically if quality delta exceeds configured threshold
Console shows per-route failover progress, priming status, and per-model quality deltas; traces link to the coordinating harmonizer requests
Automated canary (10% traffic) shows no P99 latency regression >20% before full cutover decision is applied
steps_to_validate: Create a synthetic workload (chat + long context) and snapshot baseline latency/throughput in region A
Inject a regional outage simulator (circuit at edge) to start staged failover runbook
Verify prefill probe logs show KV cache population for top-50 prefixes and measured hit-rate >=80% within prefill window
Ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic according to harmonizer policy and observe tail latency and error rates at each step
Enable model-variant fallback for the test customer, measure quality via eval set, and confirm automatic rollback when quality delta breaches threshold
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed to enumerate priming candidates from historical traffic; derived top-100 prefix list and median sequence length distribution.
2026-03-03: Prototype harmonizer control API sketched (POST /harmonizers/:id/activate) and policy schema defined; shared with PM/design for review.
2026-03-05: Wireframe dashboard columns (priming status, PV hit-rate, ramp stage, model fallback reason) posted to Drive (link in links field).
2026-03-08: Integration test harness updated to support staged traffic ramping; initial k8s job for prefill waves merged in PR #1432.

2026-03-10: End-to-end test run: prefill completed but observed KV hit-rate only 65% due to missing prefix canonicalization. Decided to add prefix normalizer in runtime path as a follow-up task (see sub_issues).
comments: Ethan: We should prioritize prefix normalization before broad rollout — the hit-rate shortfall indicates mismatched keys across regions.
Priya: Agree; creating a small follow-up to patch runtime canonicalization and add unit tests. Also scheduling a sync with Observability to add priming metrics to per-route dashboards.
Lia (SRE): Suggest throttling back ramp velocity for large customers during business hours; adding a static throttle cap to policy defaults.
Design: Dashboard mockups approved with minor copy edits; emphasis on clear failure reasons for model fallback.
QA: Need a failure injection matrix to exercise partial prefill failures and ensure rollbacks don't leave stale model pins.
